title.value: Design of Single-Atom Catalysts Anchored in N-Doped Biphenylene Using Symbolic Regression for Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia.

abstract.value: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (NO<sub>3</sub>RR) presents a synergistic strategy, achieving dual benefits in energy transformation and environmental remediation through a single process. However, the complexity of its reaction pathway and the lack of descriptors impede the rational design of high-performance NO<sub>3</sub>RR electrocatalysts. Herein, employing a series of transition metal doped and nitrogen decorated biphenylene network (TM-C<sub>x</sub>N<sub>y</sub>@BPN), an inclusive recipe toward the stability, reaction mechanism, and activity trend of single atomic catalysts (SACs) for NO<sub>3</sub>RR is proposed by integrating multidimensional insights from coordination environment, thermodynamic and electrochemical stability, Gibbs free energy profiles, electronic properties, and activity descriptors. It is revealed that the NO<sub>3</sub>RR performance of SACs is highly correlated with their local environments. Furthermore, the hybridization between the TM-3d orbitals and 2π* orbitals of NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup> gives rise to the formation of d-π* orbitals, thus promoting the NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup> activation.
